title: stalled-generation-telemetry-and-ttl-driven-snapshot-pruner
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Abrupt client disconnects and long-running stalled generations are creating state buildup in the streaming infra (prefix/KV cache, ephemeral output blobs, and functioncall in-flight state). Current heuristics either wait too long before cleanup or aggressively evict useful prefixes. This causes tail-latency spikes, unbounded ephemeral storage growth for some tenants, and increased cost for Dedicated pools.

Goal: Introduce an observability-first, TTL-driven pruner for partial generations that uses epoched telemetry to detect truly stalled generations and perform safe soft-checkpoint eviction with optional snapshotting for later resume. The design must: 1) avoid disrupting resumable generations for active clients, 2) keep storage and KV cache bounded, 3) provide clear signals for customer-facing incidents and billing, and 4) be compatible with function/tool-calling and structured output streams.

Scope: server-side streaming runtime and controller logic only (no SDK changes). We will: implement detectors, a TTL/epoch policy engine, soft-checkpoint snapshot format, and a multi-stage prune pipeline (mark->snapshot->evict).

Non-goals: client SDK request-side retries, eviction policies for Dedicated reservation reclamation (handled separately), and per-tenant billing automation in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Detector flags stalled generation within configured window (default 60s idle) without false-positive on >95% of short toolcall streams
Eviction path performs soft-checkpoint and records snapshot metadata to perf logs and listing API
KV cache reclaimed for pruned generations and peak ephemeral storage per node reduced by >=30% in the debug cluster
New telemetry metrics available in console: stalled_generation_count, prune_snapshot_size_bytes, prune_duration_ms, prune_recover_success_count
Canary rollout completed to internal org with no more than 1 P0 regressions; rollback plan tested
implementation_notes: Introduce generation_heartbeat metric emitted by the runtime for every active generation (heartbeat every 15s while active)
Epoch manager: maintain a lightweight epoch per node to categorize generations by last_activity_epoch; prune policy works on epoch gaps rather than absolute timestamp to tolerate small clock skew
Soft-checkpoint format: snapshot minimal KV prefixes + functioncall continuation token + structured-output summary; store in ephemeral object store with TTL metadata
Multi-stage prune: mark->attempt-snapshot->evict. If snapshot fails, mark generation for delayed retry and emit alert; do not evict until snapshot or retry budget exhausted
Compatibility: when functioncall is active, snapshot must include tool invocation state and any pending tool-call tokens to support resumption in client-initiated reconnect
Backpressure interaction: when a node detects upstream eviction pressure, it should prioritize in-memory prefix compaction before snapshotting to avoid I/O amplification
Config knobs (runtime config): idle_ttl_seconds, epoch_gap_threshold, snapshot_retry_budget, max_snapshot_size_bytes, should_snapshot_for_toolcalls (bool)
Data retention: default snapshot TTL 7 days for internal resumes; snapshots are deletable via admin API
Rollout plan: feature-flag gated; stage 1 internal-only (trace-level logging), stage 2 low-traffic tenants, stage 3 platform-wide
Testing: unit tests for epoch manager, integration tests with simulated abrupt disconnects and toolcall stubs, chaos test that kills SDK connections and validates recovery
updates: 2026-03-06: Initial scoping doc posted to Confluence https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Stalled+Generation+Pruner. Decided to prefer epoch gaps over absolute timestamps to minimize clock skew issues.

2026-03-08: Spike complete — prototype added generation_heartbeat metric and simple epoch manager. Observed false positives on short-lived toolcall streams; added heuristic to extend grace window for active functioncall states.

2026-03-10: Design review with PM and runtime leads (notes in doc). Agreed soft-checkpoint must include functioncall continuation tokens and structured-output skeleton to support resumable streams with deterministic prefixes.

2026-03-12: Implemented mark stage and snapshot writer (internal PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5592). Snapshot size capped at 2MB by default. Manual test shows 40% reduction in ephemeral storage after eviction sweep in dev cluster.

2026-03-14: Found race during snapshot when concurrent KV compaction runs; mitigation strategy added: snapshot obtains short-lived compaction lock, fallback to mark-only if lock cannot be obtained within 200ms. Filed separate follow-up ENG-330212 for compaction lock refactor.
comments: Marco Santos (assignee) 2026-03-07: Noted we should add customer-visible audit events so SRE and customers can see when a snapshot was taken for their generation.
Priya Mehta (PM) 2026-03-09: Request to expose prune metrics in Console usage dashboard and add an alert template for tenant storage spikes.
Jon R. (runtime lead) 2026-03-11: Concern about snapshot I/O on busy nodes; agreed to throttle snapshots and add per-node snapshot concurrency limit.
Design review comment 2026-03-10: Ensure snapshot format is forward-compatible; include schema version and model-seed hash for compatibility across runtime releases.
